A little about me / 01

Curious by nature.
Intentional by design.

I’m Suchismita — a UI/UX designer who enjoys making sense of complex things and turning them into clear, thoughtful digital experiences.

I’m drawn to the space where systems thinking meets human behaviour.

01 ORIGIN

My route into design wasn’t a straight line. I studied Biotechnology for my bachelor’s degree and later completed an MCA. Somewhere along that journey, I discovered UI design — and found a field that brought together two things I enjoy: understanding how things work and making them easier for people to use.

02 METHOD

That science background still shapes the way I approach problems. I like to observe, ask questions, look for patterns, test an assumption and improve what isn’t working. I try not to treat a screen as an isolated picture; I want to understand the need, the context and the steps around it.

03 PROOF

For 1.6 years, I worked as the sole UI/UX designer at Antro PAI Technologies. Working across multiple products taught me to take ownership and make considered decisions independently, then communicate those decisions clearly. It also taught me that good design is as much about the thinking behind it as the final interface.

04 NOW

Today, I enjoy working through the full design journey — from understanding a problem and mapping a flow to shaping the interface, documenting decisions and preparing designs for handoff. I’m continuing to deepen my UX research and usability practice, and I use case studies to make my process and reasoning visible.

03 / How I work

Thoughtful work,
from the inside out.

I value the reasoning behind a design as much as its visual finish.

01 / Understand

Start with the problem.

I try to understand who a product is for, what they need to do and where the friction lives before settling on a solution.

02 / Make sense

Bring structure to complexity.

Flows, information hierarchy and clear documentation help turn scattered requirements into something people can navigate.

03 / Refine

Care about the details.

I pay attention to consistency, useful feedback, edge cases and the small interactions that make an experience feel considered.

04 / What I believe

Design principles
I come back to.

01 / Clarity

Clarity over decoration.

Every element should have a reason to exist. Good design makes the next step feel obvious.

02 / Details

Small details matter.

Thoughtful states, useful feedback and considered micro-interactions make products feel intuitive.

03 / Curiosity

Stay curious.

Good ideas often begin with observation: asking why, noticing patterns and looking beyond the screen.

05 / Beyond the screen

There’s a world
outside the interface.

I enjoy close-up photography, especially moments in nature and the small details of creatures around me. Watching butterflies, noticing textures and waiting for the right moment gives me a different kind of creative focus — one that’s patient, observant and curious.
